researchTasks: [High] Minimum age, output ownership, platform retention, model-to-tool mapping: Please provide minimum age and consent rules for each student-facing tool, generated-output ownership terms, platform chat retention and model/provider mapping. (route: Vendor privacy/security contact; evidence wanted: Terms, DPA, subprocessor list, retention schedule, product feature matrix)

Confirm product-specific minimum age and output ownership; verify retention duration and exact AI-provider list against current subprocessor schedule; assess Australian data residency and local contractual terms.
Ask vendor (Minimum learner age): What is the minimum age for each student-facing product and what parental consent/school authorisation is required?
Ask vendor (How it responds to learners): Is the AI designed to coach learners with questions/hints, follow educator-defined behaviour, or provide direct answers? Can this be configured?
Ask vendor (Answers from your own course content): For each student-facing tool, can it answer only from teacher-supplied materials and show citations to those materials?
Ask vendor (Shows its sources): For each student-facing tool, can it answer only from teacher-supplied materials and show citations to those materials?
Ask vendor (Who owns what the AI produces): Who owns AI-generated lessons, quizzes, feedback and student outputs, and what licence does MagicSchool receive?

Researcher note (dataPrivacy), not shown until sourced: Student-data policy says third-party AI providers cannot retain child personal information or use it for model training. Applies when MagicSchool processes student data as service provider/processor for schools/customers.

Researcher note (outputOwnership), not shown until sourced: MagicSchool says student-facing access is educator-managed; outputs are drafts for educator review, not final grading. Vendor states no student data is used to train models and AI providers are contractually prohibited from retention/training.
